basis: Cataracts, alopecia/dermatitis and oral disease define syndrome; myopathy in 1/1 assessed. Developmental delay in 1/2 omitted under four-axis cap.
Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism; anosmia represents sensory loss in 12/12. Joint hypermobility in 4/13 does not establish musculoskeletal damage.
Defined by Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome and developmental delay; both supported by frequent or very frequent HPO annotations.
Distal arthrogryposis and ectodermal dysplasia define joint and skin/appendage involvement; unspecified additional anomalies do not justify further axes.
Intellectual disability and contractures/joint stiffness occur in 80-99%; ptosis/blepharophimosis and cardiovascular malformations each occur in 30-79%.
Hair/nail dysplasia and intellectual disability define syndrome, each present in 80-99%; hearing impairment occurs in only 5-29%.
Definition identifies ectodermal dysplasia, cleft lip/palate and intellectual disability. Eyelid fusion and delayed bone growth are variable without established frequency.
Vaccinia virus infection produces characteristic cutaneous lesions; occasional systemic manifestations do not establish common additional organ damage.
Hereditary abnormality of cutaneous dermatoglyphic ridges; no evidence for another organ axis.
Acute laryngeal inflammation is predominantly viral or bacterial; the larynx belongs to the pulmonary axis. Vocal strain accounts for some noninfectious cases.
Primary glial neoplasm of the central nervous system; angiocentric growth does not establish a separate vascular disease.
Developmental impairment and precocious puberty define syndrome; puberty occurs in 80-99%. Small extremities and hypermobility do not establish locomotor damage.
Bacterial toxin blocks neuromuscular and autonomic transmission. Paralysis, respiratory insufficiency and autonomic symptoms do not establish direct muscle or lung damage.
Glycine/lipoate metabolic defect causes encephalopathy, seizures and developmental delay. Liver dysfunction and cardiac defect each reported in only one assessed patient.
Both eye disease and hereditary neurological disease define this group, as supported by its parents and named subtypes.
Hepatitis delta virus directly causes liver inflammation; bleeding and confusion are occasional consequences of hepatic disease.
Autoimmune blistering disease; oral erosions occur in 80-99%, and direct airway injury with bronchiolitis obliterans in about 30%. Associated neoplasms are separate diseases.
Hypertrophic peripheral neuropathy with sensory impairment and cataracts are the defining manifestations.
Intellectual disability and seizures occur in 80-99%. Retinopathy is annotated at 5-29%; pigmentation alone and recurrent infections do not establish additional organ damage.
Defining acronym includes sebaceous/pigmented nevi and aplasia cutis, CNS malformations, and limbal dermoids.
Spinal vascular malformation and chronic venous congestion cause progressive necrotizing myelopathy; this is vascular rather than autoimmune myelitis.
Serine biosynthesis defect causes severe brain malformations and ichthyosis; limb contractures and restricted joint movement occur in most affected fetuses.
Acute myeloid malignancy of marrow and blood; CEBPA mutation does not establish another organ axis.
Corneal opacity, elbow contractures/dislocations with forearm bone hypoplasia, and intellectual/developmental impairment are defining features, annotated in 80-99%.
ENaC dysfunction causes renal salt wasting, hyperkalemia and acidosis. Respiratory infections occur in 30-79%, but alone do not establish direct pulmonary damage.
